scope: Local durable preparation and fully intercepted Chromium; no live Supabase
coverage: Callback reads its persisted command and identity after pending fsync, atomic rename and installed-file fsync
24 simultaneous intents retain every entry while all HTTP callbacks may remain in flight together
Exclusive journal ownership, reopen with original identity and chained history
Request-object deduplication and fail-closed receipt reuse with changed command
Pending-file fsync failure blocks queued and subsequent dispatch and preserves pending recovery evidence
Atomic rename failure blocks queued and subsequent dispatch and preserves pending recovery evidence
Installed-file fsync failure blocks dispatch while retaining the installed intent for reconciliation
Payload and hash-chain tampering reject reopen
Preallocated Auth principal UUID persists without email or credentials
Actual admin-users Edge route saves identity metadata and email hash without credential or arbitrary payload fields
Credential keys and Bearer values block generic command persistence
Presence, adoption and resolve_online_request are recorded writes; read allowlist and Auth-session bodies are excluded
Unknown RPC, Storage, REST, legacy archive and foreign writes abort before dispatch
Wrapped late handlers persist before fetch and distinguish errors before versus after dispatch
Chromium context protects independent pages A/B/C, reopened C and a newer context interceptor using controlled responses only
limits: Records prepared intent, not server ACK, cleanup or certification
Existing pending file or stale owner lock requires explicit recovery review
Windows tests file fsync and rename; no power-loss simulation or directory fsync
Full command content belongs in the private run journal; account command hash covers disclosed metadata only
